cards.text: Saul wants David dead, so David runs from Naioth in Ramah. And who does he run to? Jonathan, SAUL'S OWN SON, and David has some questions.

cards.question: True or false: David tells Jonathan he knows exactly what he did to make Saul want to kill him.

cards.text: Jonathan shuts that down FAST: “Far from it!” “You will not die.” And friend, he's got a reason he's so sure.

cards.question: Why is Jonathan so sure his father isn't planning to kill David?

answers.text: His father tells him everything great or small
His father has already forgiven David
His father needs David to lead the army

cards.text: But David isn't buying it. Jonathan thinks he's in every one of his dad's group chats, but according to David, there's one he's NOT in, and it's called Don't Tell Jonathan.

cards.question: David says Saul knows Jonathan favors David, so Saul keeps his plan quiet so Jonathan won't be ___.

cards.text: Then David swears it: “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer one cleanout away from the trash can, and I promise you, ONE step is closer than that.

cards.question: Jonathan says he'll do whatever David desires. So David lays out a plan: tomorrow is the New Moon, and he's supposed to dine with the king. Instead, he'll hide in the ___ until the third evening.

cards.text: If Saul misses him at all, Jonathan is to say David urgently asked to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown. There's a yearly sacrifice there for his whole clan.

cards.question: If Saul hears that and says Good, David is safe. But if Saul is enraged, what will that tell Jonathan?

answers.text: That his father has evil intentions
That his father just needs more time
That his father feels insulted by David

cards.text: David calls himself Jonathan's servant and asks Jonathan to show him kindness. After all, Jonathan brought him into a covenant before the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: David says that if there's iniquity in him, Jonathan should kill him himself instead of bringing him to Saul.

cards.text: “Never!” Jonathan says. Of course he'd tell David. Then David asks the real question: “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”

cards.question: Before Jonathan answers David's question about who will tell him, where does Jonathan take David?

cards.text: Out in the field, Jonathan swears by the LORD, the God of Israel, that he'll sound out his father by tomorrow or the next day. If Saul is favorable toward David, Jonathan will send for him and tell him.

cards.question: And if Saul means to bring evil on David, what does Jonathan swear he'll do?

answers.text: Tell David and send him away safely
Bring David to plead with the king
Stand guard over David's hiding place

cards.text: Then Jonathan blesses him: “May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.” And he asks David to treat him with the LORD's loving devotion as long as he lives.

cards.question: Jonathan has one more request. True or false: Jonathan asks David never to cut off his loving devotion from Jonathan's household, not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David's enemies.

cards.text: So Jonathan makes a covenant with the house of David. And then he has David reaffirm his vow.

cards.question: Why does Jonathan have David reaffirm his vow?

answers.text: Out of fear of his father

cards.text: Jonathan isn't done planning. Tomorrow is the New Moon, and David's seat will be empty, so he WILL be missed.

cards.question: After three days, David is to hurry down to the place he hid when this trouble began. What should he wait beside?

cards.text: Jonathan will shoot three arrows to the side of the stone, as if aiming at a target, then send a boy to find them. Friend, this man is about to send a text message with ARROWS.

cards.question: If Jonathan tells the boy, “Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,” what does that mean for David?

answers.text: It is safe to come out
He should wait one more day

cards.question: True or false: If Jonathan tells the boy the arrows are beyond him, David must go, because the LORD has sent him away.

cards.text: Jonathan seals it: the LORD is a witness between them forever. So David hides in the field, and the New Moon comes.

Saul sits in his usual seat by the wall, across from Jonathan and beside Abner, the commander of his army (1 Samuel 14:50). And David's seat? EMPTY, and nothing at a dinner table talks louder than an empty chair.

cards.question: On that first day, Saul says nothing about David's empty seat. What does Saul think happened to David?

answers.text: Something made him too sick to come
Something called him back to Ramah

cards.text: Day two, and David's seat is STILL empty, so Saul asks Jonathan why the son of Jesse hasn't come to the meal. Notice he doesn't say David's name, and friend, I don't love that.

cards.question: True or false: Jonathan tells Saul that David asked permission to go to his clan's sacrifice in Bethlehem.

cards.text: Then Saul's anger burns against Jonathan. He insults Jonathan's mother and says Jonathan has chosen the son of Jesse to his own shame.

cards.question: Saul tells Jonathan that as long as the son of Jesse lives, neither Jonathan nor his ___ will be established.

cards.text: Then Saul orders him, “Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”

cards.question: True or false: When Saul orders Jonathan to bring David to him, Jonathan agrees to do it.
Jonathan asks his father why David must be put to death and what he has done. What does Saul do next?

answers.text: He hurls his spear at Jonathan
He orders guards to seize Jonathan
He storms away from the table

cards.text: Now Jonathan knows his father is determined to kill David. He gets up from the table in fierce anger and doesn't eat any food that second day of the month.

cards.question: Why does Jonathan go without food that second day?

answers.text: He's grieved by how his father treated David
He's too afraid to stay near his father
He's ashamed of covering for David

cards.text: Next morning, Jonathan goes out to the field for his appointment with David, and a small boy comes with him. Jonathan tells the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.”

cards.question: Remember the signal. As the boy runs, where does Jonathan's arrow land?

answers.text: On this side of the boy

cards.text: Then Jonathan cries out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” Three ways to say GO, which is exactly me when the timer goes off and my cookies are still in the oven.

cards.question: The boy picks up the arrow and brings it back to Jonathan. True or false: the boy knows all about the arrangement between Jonathan and David.

cards.text: Jonathan hands the boy his gear and sends him back to the city. Then David gets up from the south side of the stone, falls facedown and bows three times.

cards.question: David and Jonathan kiss each other and ___ together, though David does it more.
Before David leaves, what does Jonathan tell him?

answers.text: Go in peace since they swore in the LORD's name
Stay hidden here until Saul calms down
Come back to the king's table in three days

cards.text: Then David gets up and leaves, and Jonathan goes back into the city. That's where we'll leave these two for now, friend, but this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: David and Saul first show up here, but neither is said simply to be who they are. Saul is never named as king of Israel, and David is given no description.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The setup for this choice is told only inside the question, not on a story card. That setup is Jonathan's promise to do whatever David desires (v4), the New Moon and the dinner with the king (v5). Verse 4 never appears on any story card, and the question carries several beats.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out because it is the only one in Bible-sounding wording ("swore in the LORD's name"). One wrong answer sounds modern ("until Saul calms down").

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The question is in present tense ("David and Jonathan kiss each other and ___ together, though David does it more"), but the answers are all past tense (wept, laughed, sang). The filled-in sentence doesn't read correctly.
findings.question: Should fill-in-the-blank answers have to match the grammar and tense of the question's sentence? If so, should that become a rule in prep-walkthrough.md (for example under Question types or Answer rules)?
